statuses.partial: Works with a difference, explained in the note
statuses.missing: Should exist here and doesn't yet
statuses.not-possible: This platform can't do it, explained in the note

features.name: Dark and Clear logos use one ink
Light clock cards, dark on the screensaver
features.note: Lite has no card clock.

features.name: Focused name clears the focus ring
Focus glow surrounds the tile; background glow on Dark and Clear only
features.note: Samsung's focus glow has no app color. Android Lite draws no focus glow, by the owner's choice; on Auto a TV low only on memory (Fire TV Stick 4K) keeps it while the wallpaper is still.

features.name: Date, caption and news stay readable over bright video
features.note: Android has darker shadows (1.67-mh24), not yet looked at on a TV.

features.name: A stalled wallpaper gives way to the next
features.note: Android skips after 30 s of buffering (1.67-mh24), not yet tried on a TV.

features.name: Focus Style: Standard, High Contrast, Invert
features.note: Lite has no Invert. Built in from the web page, not yet looked at on a Samsung.

features.name: Focus Glow: Small, Medium, Large
features.note: Android Lite draws no glow, so the row is hidden there; on Auto the Fire TV Stick 4K keeps the glow and the row while the wallpaper is still, and loses both while it moves. Built in from the web page, not yet looked at on a Samsung.

features.name: Wallpaper Tint: Off, Dim, Warm, Cool
features.note: Built in from the web page, not yet looked at on a Samsung.

features.name: Apps per Row
features.note: Web offers 4 to 6 and keeps its default of 6; Android defaults to 5. Built in from the web page, not yet looked at on a Samsung.

features.name: One or Two Rows on Home
features.note: Built in from the web page, not yet looked at on a Samsung.

features.name: Peek at Next Row
features.note: The web dock lifts and the next row shows 46 units tall below it, with a toggle in Personalize (index.src.html layout()). Not yet looked at on a Samsung.

features.name: Dock, in Appearance, for every tile style (fainter behind Clear)
features.note: Built into the Samsung page, not yet looked at on a Samsung. Tried on the SHIELD.

features.name: Home Mode replaces Effects
features.note: On webOS, Auto behaves as Full, and Efficient is the old Lite. There are no wallpaper or glass changes. Built in from the web page, not yet looked at on a Samsung.

features.name: Clock Style is Cards and Plain
features.note: Built in from the web page, not yet looked at on a Samsung.

features.name: Passcode by arrow keys
features.note: Built in from the web page, not yet looked at on a Samsung.

features.name: Logos set their own size
features.note: Built in from the web page, not yet looked at on a Samsung.

features.name: Color plates deepen until white logos reach 4.5:1
features.note: Built in from the web page, not yet looked at on a Samsung.

features.name: Settings gear with a lit hub
features.note: Built in from the web page; not yet looked at on a Samsung.

features.name: Frosted dock and grid over video
features.note: Lite draws flat panels. Built in, but left out of the LEAN build; not yet looked at on a Samsung.

features.name: Liquid Glass
features.note: Needs Android 13 shaders.

features.name: A tile for each input
features.note: No app can open Samsung's Source panel, so the Inputs tile is gone and Source takes two presses. The Control Center Inputs row is removed on Samsung from mh35, as no input list reaches a web app.

features.name: Turn Off TV in Control Center
features.note: Android has it from mh35 through Home Guard (an accessibility service): standby on Android 9+, else the TV's power menu. No row where the guard is not bound: on Fire OS 6 the guard build installs but Fire OS never binds its accessibility service (dumpsys accessibility lists none), so FireKeeper keeps Home in front instead. Samsung web apps can turn the screen off but not the TV, so the row is removed.

features.name: Home button opens Home
features.note: Samsung opens Smart Hub first, then Home reopens over it. Only from Home's own screen, on both Samsungs. Not from inside apps.

features.name: Phone page: scan a QR code to pick wallpaper, send photos, name the city
features.note: A Tizen web app can't listen on the network. On webOS, home-svc could serve it.

features.name: Give an app's tile a picture of your own
features.note: Android sends the picture from the phone page, so the web builds need that first or another way in.

features.name: Wallpaper and screensaver sources: Aerial, Photos, Clock, Videos, System
features.note: The web builds offer Aerial videos and Plex videos or photos.

features.name: Aerial Quality: Auto, 1080p, 4K, Dolby Vision
features.note: LG offers 1080p and 4K (HEVC), not Dolby Vision, and 4K is untried on an LG. Samsung stalls above 1080p H.264, so the row is removed.

features.name: Spoken labels for screen readers
features.note: Needs a check that webOS and Tizen screen readers read an app page at all.

features.name: Chinese calendar date beside the clock on Chinese-language TVs
features.note: The web Home is English only, so there is no Chinese-language mode to show it in.

features.name: Control Center buttons: Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Settings, your VPN app (once a VPN has been up; blue while on), Auto/Dark/Light
features.note: The web Control Center is a list. It has Network, Settings and an Appearance row, but no Bluetooth row (no known way to open LG's or Samsung's Bluetooth page) and no VPN app. Samsung's version is built in and not yet looked at on a TV.

features.name: Brightness row only where it works
features.note: Android hides it on boxes and sticks (no inputs and no panel it knows), where the setting moves nothing, and keeps it on every TV. LG's row opens Picture Settings; Samsung's is removed (its Settings row opens the same menu).

features.name: Lit glass edge: light from the top left, a faint reflection bottom right
features.note: Android bakes glisse's rim per size; the web draws it as two inset rings on the dock, panels, pill and glass tiles.

features.name: Bluetooth opens the remotes and accessories page
features.note: Google TV opens Remotes & Accessories (tried on the onn 4K: Connected Devices). Android 12 TV settings open it as a slice (checked only by what answers the intent, on a Hisense). SHIELD and other Android 11 and older TVs can't open that page alone, so it opens the pairing search (tried on the SHIELD).

features.name: Inputs only where inputs can be switched
features.note: Android hides it on boxes and sticks, counting only inputs with hardware behind them. LG and Samsung are TVs.

features.name: Glass in glisse's numbers: tint, 1.5 saturation, 1.22 rim, 0.5 edge, press springs
features.note: Android 9 to 12 draw glisse's tint, saturation, rim and outline. Android 13 and later keep the lens shader's own rim, without the saturation. The web has no live blur, so its frost is baked with the saturation, and panels stay opaque so tiles don't show through; its rim is an even ring. Press uses glisse's spring; focus stays critically damped on every build, because an overshoot made the focus ring shimmer.

features.name: Clear Light appearance: less white, more picture, wallpaper dimmed 12%
features.note: Built into the web page, not yet looked at on an LG or a Samsung.

features.name: Wallpaper Tint for each appearance: Dark starts on Dim, which replaces Dark's own dimming
features.note: Light starts on a lighter Dim. A tint chosen before carries over to both. Samsung's is built in and not yet looked at on a TV.

features.name: Every app's focused tile glows: white for grey or black-and-white apps, dark brand colors lifted, a logo's own glow color
features.note: Samsung's is built in, not yet looked at on a TV.

features.name: Status pill shows the network name
features.note: Android from mh35: 14sp name, 18dp icon, 30dp pill, smaller than the time beside it; "Wi-Fi" when Android withholds the name, "Not Connected" offline, matching the web.

features.name: A moving wallpaper slows to a stop under a menu and picks up again, and the glass fades through its lens
features.note: The web builds pause their video without easing; their glass is baked frost, which doesn't change under a menu.

features.name: When the TV Turns On
features.note: A Samsung web app cannot open anything when the TV turns on (the Tizen adapter has no boot target), so the row and its page are removed there from mh35.

features.name: VPN badge and VPN button while a VPN is up
features.note: LG and Samsung web apps cannot see the TV's VPN state, and neither TV runs VPN apps.

features.name: Rename a folder and move an app out of it
features.note: Web from mh35: Rename Folder types on the TV keyboard; hold OK on an app inside a folder for Move Out of Folder or Hide.

features.name: Aerial categories (Landscapes, Cities, Space, Underwater)
features.note: Android from mh35, in the Screensaver section; the last one on stays on. Applies to the wallpaper and screensaver.

features.name: Screensaver clock drifts against burn-in
features.note: Samsung (no CSS variables) drifts by an inline transform from mh35.

features.name: Focus tilt and sheen
features.note: Android Lite drops both; webOS has tilt only; Samsung's Chromium M47 has neither.

features.name: Plex sees the right device
features.note: Samsung says Tizen / Samsung TV from mh35 instead of LG TV.

features.name: Inter typeface
features.note: Android 7 and older (Fire TV Stick 4K) get four static Inter weights from mh35 instead of Roboto. The web builds use the TV's own fonts.

features.name: Text size matches across Android devices
features.note: Fire OS ships its text size at 1.0, Google TV and SHIELD at 0.85; Home reads Fire OS against 1.0 from mh35.

features.name: Hidden Apps
Passcode for settings
Interface sounds
features.note: Android has TV, Home and Off; the web builds have on and off.

features.name: Weather condition, city and units
features.note: Android's corner clock leaves out the condition and long city names; its big clock has them with H and L.

features.name: Uninstall from a tile
features.note: Samsung web apps cannot uninstall apps, so the row is removed.
